guide_zh.overview: Free, local plugin that keeps tool output out of your coding agent's context window. Sandbox and SQLite FTS5 search, 99% fewer bytes in context. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI and 4 more agents. Zero telemetry.

readme.markdown:
# Context Mode **A free, local plugin for 10 coding agents. It keeps tool output out of your agent's context window and keeps all usage data on your machine. The plugin is free forever.** [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/context-mode?label=npm%20downloads)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/context-mode) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/mksglu/context-mode?style=flat&color=yellow)](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/1478479412700909750?label=Discord&logo=discord&color=5865f2)](https://discord.gg/DCN9jUgN5v) [![License: ELv2](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ELv2-blue.svg)](LICENSE) **33K GitHub stars · 683K npm downloads** (read 2026-11-01, [stats.json](stats.json)) · on the Hacker News front page and GitHub Trending: [charts and sources](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) > The Context Mode plugin is free and local, with its source open on GitHub. **Context Mode Gateway** is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It takes the same idea from tool output to the whole conversation: Gateway Recall keeps long sessions searchable, and Gateway Memory shares what your agents learn across sessions and tools. [See how the Gateway works](https://contextmode.ai/docs/how-saving-works?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=quote) **Contents:** [Why](#why) · [Adoption](#adoption-stars-and-npm-downloads) · [Install](#install) · [Try it](#try-it) · [Use cases](#use-cases) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Tools](#tools) · [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) · [Context Mode Gateway](#context-mode-gateway) · [License](#license) · [Community](#community) ## Why A coding agent reads files, runs commands and fetches pages, and every result goes into its context window. The Context Mode plugin runs that work in a local sandbox, keeps the full output in a SQLite index on your machine, and gives the agent the part it asks for. - **The plugin is free forever.** Use it at home and at work, free of charge, under a source-available license. - **Runs on your machine.** The hooks, the sandbox and search run as local processes next to your agent. - **The plugin keeps your data on your machine.** Every index lives in `~/.context-mode`: one `context.db` per project. - **Zero telemetry.** The plugin keeps all usage data on your machine. [Security and privacy](#security-and-privacy) lists each network call it makes. - **Works offline after install.** Sandbox runs, file indexing and search use local SQLite and your own runtimes. - **Thinking in Code.** The agent writes a short script instead of reading the data, and only what the script prints reaches the context: see [How it works, step 5](#thinking-in-code). - **Small replies.** On the 36 bench rows with 10 KB or more of raw output, the plugin's median reply is 99.4% smaller than the raw output. ## Adoption: stars and npm downloads
Open the [interactive chart](https://contextmode.ai/open-source/stats?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=adoption#daily) and point at a bar to read its value. Tabs there show days, weeks, months and years. Stars come from the GitHub GraphQL API (`starredAt`); npm downloads come from `api.npmjs.org/downloads/range`. The total up to 2026-10-29 is 683K npm downloads (`stats.json` keeps a daily copy). A daily job redraws both charts. - **Hacker News.** "MCP server that reduces Claude Code context consumption by 98%" reached the front page with 570+ points and 107 comments on 2026-02-28 ([thread](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47193064)). - **GitHub Trending.** A bot that watches GitHub Trending logged the repo there on 14 days from 2026-04-24 to 2026-10-17 ([uibm/trending-watcher](https://github.com/uibm/trending-watcher/issues?q=%22mksglu%2Fcontext-mode%22)). Starred by engineers at these companies: each name is the company field of 2 or more stargazer profiles, read with the GitHub GraphQL API on 2026-11-01 ([data](docs/assets/readme/data/stargazer-companies.json)). ## Install Pick your agent: [Claude Code](#install-claude-code) · [Codex](#install-codex) · [Gemini CLI](#install-gemini) · [Qwen Code](#install-qwen) · [Pi](#install-pi) · [OpenCode](#install-opencode) · [Copilot CLI](#install-copilot-cli) · [Kiro](#install-kiro) · [VS Code](#install-vscode) · [ZCode](#install-zcode) Open its block and copy its own install command. Each block also holds the update, check and remove steps, and the [Install guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/install?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install) walks through them. The plugin needs Node 24.15.0 or later, from the engines field in [package.json](package.json). On Windows, add Git for Windows: the shell tools run in Git Bash, and doctor checks for it. contextmode installs as the npm package and command `context-mode`. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code install from GitHub, and each of their commands names the release branch.

Kiro ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents kiro ``` ```sh # update context-mode upgrade # check context-mode doctor --agents kiro # remove context-mode setup --remove --agents kiro ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
VS Code (Copilot) ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup --agents vscode ``` ```sh # update context-mode upgrade # check context-mode doctor --agents vscode # remove context-mode setup --remove --agents vscode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
ZCode ```sh zcode plugins marketplace add mksglu/context-mode zcode plugins install context-mode@context-mode ``` ```sh # update zcode plugins update context-mode@context-mode # check zcode plugins list # remove zcode plugins uninstall context-mode@context-mode ``` Hooks ✓ (hook file) · MCP ✓ · Skills ✓
The npm route works for every agent: ```sh npm i -g context-mode context-mode setup ``` Setup is also the repair. It shows a plan, saves your earlier config, then applies the plan; when a step ends early, it restores the saved config. To uninstall: ```sh context-mode setup --remove npm rm -g context-mode ``` Restart the agent, then run `/ctx-doctor` in it. Each check prints PASS or a fix command, and the [Doctor guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/doctor?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-doctor) explains each check.
How we tested the install Every agent gets hooks, the MCP server and the plugin skills; the last line of each block above says how. Hooks reach each agent in one of three ways: in the plugin package (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code), in a hook file (Codex, Copilot CLI, Kiro, VS Code, ZCode), or in a plugin inside the agent (OpenCode, Pi). The [Agents guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/agents?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-agents) shows what each agent runs. We ran the real binary of each agent with the plugin hook: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi, OpenCode, Copilot CLI and ZCode. Each run used a clean temp home and a local test model, on 2.0.0-next.15. For VS Code and Kiro, the check covers the hook setup: VS Code runs the hook command with the documented payload, and kiro-cli 2.35.2 loads all 6 hook entries. CI runs setup, doctor, a hook and an MCP handshake for all 10 agents from the packed package on Linux, macOS and Windows. Record: [HOOKS-FIRE.md](docs/architecture/release/HOOKS-FIRE.md). Each agent uses its own install command, and [ADR-0023](docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0023-native-install.md) says why.
Your first task with the plugin, step by step: [First session](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/first-session?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=install-next). Or paste a prompt from [Try it](#try-it) right now. ## Try it Paste one of these prompts into your agent after the install. Each one ran once, live, in Claude Code 2.1.312, and its answer matched the source data ([evidence and rerun steps](bench/evidence/try-it-2026-11-02/README.md)). The headline numbers in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) use the median of 5 runs. Other agents do the same job with the same tools: `ctx_execute`, `ctx_index` and `ctx_search`. After a prompt, run the stats skill and read the report yourself ([See the saving](#see-the-saving)). ```text On https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect, show me the example that connects to a chat server and cleans up, and list the rules for the dependency array. ``` The hook sends WebFetch to the sandbox, and the agent searches the page for the example and the rules. 601,984 B raw, 20,860 B reached the context, 96.5% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). ```text Fetch https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/photos. Which photo has the longest title (give its id and title), and how many photos have a title that contains the word "est"? ``` The agent runs code over 5,000 JSON records in the sandbox and gets back two answers. 1,039,898 B raw, 393 B reached the context, 99.96% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). The answer is two short facts, so this is the best case of the four. ```text Here is a Linux syslog sample: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/logpai/loghub/master/Linux/Linux_2k.log. How many authentication failures does it contain, and which 3 remote hosts caused the most? ``` The agent counts failures in a 1,999-line syslog in the sandbox. 216,485 B raw, 566 B reached the context, 99.7% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). ```text What are the top 10 stories on the Hacker News front page right now? Give title, points and domain for each. ``` The hook sends WebFetch to the sandbox, and the agent reads ten stories from the page. 35,087 B raw, 1,501 B reached the context, 95.7% saved (2026-11-02, 2.0.0-next.26, claude-haiku-5-5). The front page changes, so the raw size changes with each run. ### See the saving Run the stats skill right after a prompt. It needs plain Node and runs offline; [bench/README.md](bench/README.md) lists each scenario and its options. Method, data files and rerun steps: [Benchmarks guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/benchmarks?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=benchmarks). ### Longer sessions Say you debug a slow test all afternoon. The agent reads files, runs the suite and fetches docs, and each result goes into the context window. When the window is full, the host compacts it, and from then on the agent sees a short summary plus your next message. Context Mode keeps the full output of each large tool call in `context.db` on your machine and gives the agent a small reply. At compaction, a snapshot of at most 2,048 B keeps the session state. After the compaction, the agent calls `ctx_resume` to read that snapshot back and `ctx_search` to find any earlier output by keyword. In the bench, a scripted session of 40 tool outputs and one compaction made a 442,893 B transcript, and the `ctx_resume` block that brought the agent back was 2,019 B (row `e-long-session` in the bench file; [open the case](bench/e-continuity/README.md#e-long-session)). In the same bench, one large log of 666,796 B put 3,380 B into the context, and the full log stayed in the index for `ctx_search` (row `d-synth-1m`; [open the case](bench/d-externalize/README.md#d-synth-1m)). How the snapshot picks what to keep: the [Long sessions guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/long-sessions?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=longer-sessions) and [ADR-0009](docs/architecture/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md). ### Speed Median of 5 runs, bench of 2026-11-01. | Measure | Result | |---|---| | Hook time over a bare `node` start, per agent | 7.5 ms to 12.3 ms | | `ctx_search`, 20 queries over 8 indexed files | 1.62 ms median, 6.70 ms max | | `ctx_index`, 3 real files, 625,649 B | 150 ms per MB | Source: rows `g-hook-kiro` to `g-hook-claude-code`, `g-search-latency` and `g-index-per-mb` of [the bench file](bench/results/2026-11-01-darwin-arm64.md), with every agent and query. The [overhead cases](bench/g-overhead/README.md) show how each one runs. Next, what happens inside one tool call, in [How it works](#how-it-works). ## How it works One tool call, in time order, from the install to a hook error. 1. **Install.** Each agent's own install command adds the MCP server, the hooks and the skills `ctx-doctor`, `ctx-stats` and `ctx-upgrade` to that agent's config folder, for example `~/.codex/skills//SKILL.md`. `context-mode setup` writes or repairs any part the native command leaves out ([ADR-0023](docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0023-native-install.md)). 2. **Session start.** The `SessionStart` hook opens the project database. When the session ran before, the agent gets one line that tells it to call `ctx_resume` ([dispatch.ts](src/core/hooks/dispatch.ts)). 3. **PreToolUse checks.** Before a tool runs, the `PreToolUse` hook checks the call in a fixed order: the user's deny list, WebFetch, curl and wget, inline HTTP and build commands, then a full-file Read over `OUTPUT_CAP` (16,384 B) and one-file shell dumps such as `cat` or `tail`. A Read with a line range runs as usual ([decide.ts](src/core/policy/decide.ts)). 4. **The exact call.** When a check matches, the hook stops the call and its reply names the exact `ctx_*` call to use, for example `ctx_execute` with `{"language":"shell","code":"","intent":""}`. For WebFetch the reply names `ctx_index`, then `ctx_search` ([read-deny.ts](src/core/policy/read-deny.ts)). 5. **The sandbox.** This is the Thinking in Code step: the agent's script runs here, and only what it prints comes back. `ctx_execute` writes the script to a temp folder and spawns the runtime from an argument list in the project folder. The timeout is `EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` (600,000 ms, default and maximum); on timeout it stops the whole process group (`taskkill /F /T` on Windows). The child gets your environment minus preload variables such as `NODE_OPTIONS`, and the agent gets what the script prints, at most `OUTPUT_CAP` ([execute.ts](src/core/tools/execute.ts)). **Thinking in Code.** The agent sends a short script as a tool parameter, the script reads the data in the sandbox, and only what it prints goes into the context. Two real calls, in the form the Claude Code terminal shows them: `ctx_execute` on 5,000 JSON records, from the Claude Code 2.1.312 stream of the Try-it run with Context Mode 2.0.0-next.26 ([04-api-json.json](bench/evidence/try-it-2026-11-02/04-api-json.json)). The data is 1,039,898 B; the agent gets 254 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_execute (MCP)(language: "javascript", c…jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/photos\"); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\"HTTP \" + res.status); const photos = await res.json(); let longest = null; for (const p of photos) { if (!longest || p.title.length > longest.title.length) longest = p; } const withEst = photos.filter(p => p.title.includes(\"est\")).length; const ties = photos.filter(p => p.title.length === longest.title.length).map(p => p.id); console.log(JSON.stringify({ total: photos.length, longest…nd count of titles containing \"est\"") ⎿ exit 0 · 239 B { "total": 5000, "longest": { "id": 653, "title": "temporibus commodi et fugit doloremque re…rit exercitationem necessitatibus aut", "length": 86 }, "longestTieIds": [ 653 ], "titlesContainingEst": 892 } ``` `ctx_batch` on an install log and a long git log, one live MCP call to `release-out/server.mjs` of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([2026-11-03-ctx-batch.json](bench/evidence/thinking-in-code/2026-11-03-ctx-batch.json)). The commands print 228,881 B; the agent gets 8,667 B, the parts that match its two queries, and the full output stays in the index. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_batch (MCP)(commands: ["cat npm-install… queries: ["cache miss","feat commit"]) ⎿ ## cache miss js.org/@esbuild%2fwin32-x64 282ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2flinux-s390x 79ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fopenbsd-x64 101ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fwin32-arm64 99ms (cache miss) npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry.npmjs.org/@esbuild%2fdarwin-arm64 99ms (cache miss) … +95 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` 6. **Indexing.** The full output goes into the index in chunks of at most `MAX_CHUNK_BYTES` (4,096 B). A Markdown chunk stays inside one heading section, and a code block that fits stays whole. Each chunk goes into two SQLite FTS5 tables: a Porter-stemmed table for words and a trigram table for paths, names and parts of words ([fts.ts](src/core/store/fts.ts)). `ctx_index` on a copy of this repo's `docs/how-it-works.md`, one live MCP call to `release-out/server.mjs` of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([calls.json](bench/evidence/terminal-calls-2026-11-03/calls.json)). The file is 11,577 B; the agent gets 64 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_index (MCP)(path: "how-it-works.md") ⎿ Indexed 1 source(s), 17 chunk(s) from s1. Label: how-it-works.md ``` 7. **Search.** `ctx_search` ranks each table with BM25 and joins the two lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion: a hit scores 1/(`RRF_K` + rank), with `RRF_K` = 60. Before it returns an empty list, it tries a spelling fix from the indexed words. Search covers this session, this worktree (the default) or the whole project, and each snippet is at most `SNIPPET_MAX_BYTES` (800 B) ([search.ts](src/core/tools/search.ts)). `ctx_search` on that index, in the same run, in a project that also holds an `AGENTS.md`. One search reads the index and every agent's memory files. The agent gets 1,268 B: one content hit and one memory hit, each with its source and heading. For memory shared across machines, agents and sessions, see [Context Mode Gateway Memory](https://contextmode.ai/docs/memory?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=search-memory). ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_search (MCP)(queries: ["compaction state block"]) ⎿ Query "compaction state block": how-it-works.md #14: ### Session continuity The hooks log each prompt, edit, command, tool error, i…e same rows always give the same bytes. memory AGENTS.md #0: # Agent rules … +10 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` 8. **Run, then replace.** On hosts that run the tool first, the `PostToolUse` hook checks the result. Output over `REPLACE_TRIGGER_BYTES` (4,096 B) goes into the index whole, and the agent gets the best-matching chunks and one `ctx_search` line for the rest ([dispatch.ts](src/core/hooks/dispatch.ts)). 9. **Journal and compaction.** The hooks log each prompt, edit, command, tool error and decision in a journal. After a compaction the agent gets a state block of at most `STATE_BUDGET` (2,048 B), and each long line becomes a `ctx_resume(seq)` pointer to the full row; one `ctx_resume` reply is at most `RESUME_CAP` (2,048 B). On the next prompt, a prompt-match block brings back the journal rows that match it by BM25 ([ADR-0009](docs/architecture/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md)). `ctx_resume` with empty parameters returns the state block, in the same run: 209 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_resume (MCP)() ⎿ indexed how-it-works.md source s1: how-it-works.md (11536 B) more: ctx_search(queries:[], scope:"session") ``` 10. **The database.** Each project has one `context.db` under `~/.context-mode`, in Node's built-in `node:sqlite`. The database runs in WAL mode and runs a PASSIVE checkpoint on close. A new database gets built under a temp name and moves into place in one atomic step, and the busy timeout is `DB_TIMEOUT_MS` (5,000 ms) ([db.ts](src/core/store/db.ts)). 11. **A hook error.** A hook always ends with exit 0. On any error it gives the host's allow reply and writes one log line to `~/.context-mode/hook-errors.log`, so your agent keeps working. A spawned hook has `HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` (5,000 ms) ([fallback.ts](src/core/hooks/fallback.ts)). Every number with its reason: [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). The rules the hook follows: [ADR-0008](docs/architecture/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md). Next, the [Tools](#tools) the agent calls. ## Tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `ctx_execute` | Runs code or a shell command in a sandbox; returns what it prints | | `ctx_batch` | Runs many commands, indexes the output, and searches it in one call | | `ctx_index` | Indexes a file, a text or a URL into the project database | | `ctx_search` | Searches the local index; returns the matching parts | | `ctx_resume` | Returns the plugin's local state block (at most 2,048 B), or one full row by `seq` | | `ctx_stats` | Shows how much output stayed out of context | | `ctx_doctor` | Checks the install; each check prints PASS or a fix command | | `ctx_upgrade` | Installs, upgrades or uninstalls; replaces old contextmode entries | | `ctx_purge` | Deletes indexed data by session, source or project | Three more real calls, from the same live run of Context Mode 2.0.0-next.36 on 2026-11-03 ([calls.json](bench/evidence/terminal-calls-2026-11-03/calls.json)). `ctx_stats`: the agent gets 3,097 B, the first line is the summary. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_stats (MCP)() ⎿ ctx_stats: 82.5% kept out all-time, 82.5% this session. … +59 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` `ctx_doctor` after `context-mode setup --agents claude-code`: 862 B, one row per check. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_doctor (MCP)() ⎿ Environment: context-mode 2.0.0-next.36 (8facf27), agent claude-code 0 (client r20-live) Environment: darwin-arm64, Node v26.8.1, shell /bin/zsh | Check | Status | Detail | Fix | |---|---|---|---| | D1 version | PASS | 2.0.0-next.36 (8facf27): ahead of next on npm (2.0.0-next.34) | | | D2 node | PASS | ok | | … +11 lines (ctrl+o to expand) ``` `ctx_purge` deletes one source: 66 B. ```text ⏺ context-mode - ctx_purge (MCP)(source: "how-it-works.md") ⎿ ctx_purge: deleted 18 rows (scope: source). This cannot be undone. ``` Full reference: [Tools](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=tools). Commands in the agent: `/ctx-stats` shows the `ctx_stats` result, `/ctx-doctor` runs `ctx_doctor` (send its report with a defect report), and `/ctx-upgrade` runs `ctx_upgrade`, then `ctx_doctor`. ## Security and privacy - The plugin keeps all its data on your machine, one database per project in `~/.context-mode`, and `ctx_purge` deletes it by session, source or project. Read the [Security guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/security?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=security). - The plugin has zero telemetry: usage data, events and crash reports stay on your machine. It uses the network for four calls, each one started by you or your agent: | Call | When | File | |---|---|---| | Fetch of a URL, for `ctx_index` | Your agent asks for a page. The fetch blocks private and link-local addresses, checks each address the host name points to, connects to the address it checked, and checks again at each redirect. | [fetch.ts](src/core/sandbox/fetch.ts) | | One read of the npm dist-tags, with `git ls-remote` of the release tags as the fallback | You run `context-mode doctor`, to check for a new version | [doctor-env.ts](src/core/ops/doctor-env.ts) | | `npm i -g context-mode`, or `gh issue create` | You run `context-mode upgrade`, or you press a key to send the debug report | [commands.ts](src/cli/commands.ts) | | Your agent's own install command, npm or git | You install or update | Your agent | - The guard test D-PRIVACY-NET-1 in [tests/0008-enforcement.test.mjs](tests/0008-enforcement.test.mjs) scans the source for HTTP clients, sockets, DNS lookups, git network calls and gh or npm spawns. It flags each new call site, so this table stays true. - Doctor and the debug report remove secrets by their structure before they print. Code from `ctx_execute` runs on your host as your user, with your files, your network and your environment except the preload variables, so keep your agent's own permission prompts on. Here "sandbox" means the output stays in the sandbox and out of the context. What the plugin stores, where, and how to delete it: [Privacy](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/privacy?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=privacy). ## Context Mode Gateway The plugin works on tool output, on your machine, and it is complete on its own. Context Mode Gateway is a separate hosted service with its own account and subscription. It works on every request, across all your agents. Its 11 features, the full list: Context Saving, Recall, Memory, Skills, Search, Session resume, Active Context, Instructions, Protect, Prompt caching, Live and Analytics. Add the Gateway when you want savings on every request, memory across sessions and agents, or cost reports for a team. For one project on one machine, the plugin covers the job. The two work together: [Gateway guide](https://contextmode.ai/docs/engine/gateway?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_content=gateway). Gateway Recall, Search and Session resume run on the Gateway server, across sessions and agents. The plugin's `ctx_search` and `ctx_resume` read the local `context.db` of one project. With the Gateway on, your requests pass through its server; the plugin keeps its own data on your machine. | Product | Runs | Scope | Billing | |---|---|---|---| | Context Mode plugin | On your machine | One project, local `context.db` | Free | | Context Mode Gateway | Hosted service | All sessions and agents | Subscription, separate from the plugin | Set up the Gateway with one command: ```sh npx @context-mode/cli ``` `npx @context-mode/cli` signs you in to your Gateway account, which has its own subscription, and writes one config change per agent. Apps: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Codex Desktop, T3 Code, OpenCode and Pi. The Gateway CLI needs Node 20.12 or later, from its npm engines field. **Live.** One session as it runs: money saved this session, bytes kept out per request, history kept and sent, and a feed of each request with its cost and saving.
